title: A 62-mooring short-window test did not resolve the July 2020 DOISST mean step
abstract: We tested whether short records at moorings can constrain the DOISST v2.1 mean step on 7 July 2020. We used archived daily product-minus-buoy residuals at a fixed sample of 62 stations. Separate linear fits over 60 days on each side gave a mean jump of +0.045 C. Joint spatial and temporal block resampling gave an interval of -0.124 to +0.163 C. The estimate changed from +0.073 C with 30-day windows to -0.003 C with 90-day windows. Station medians and separate network tests also did not resolve the sign. Calendar controls in 14 other years gave local jumps from -0.100 to +0.129 C. The joint interval was 1.97 times as wide as the spatial-only interval. This finite mooring design cannot choose the size of a global mean correction. It does not refute the satellite-input evidence for the step. Buoys are product inputs, the sample is not an ocean-area sample, and the resampling intervals are conditional summaries rather than calibrated discontinuity confidence intervals.

display.caption: Fixed-sample window tests, matched calendar controls, and centered daily residuals. Intervals resample spatial groups and temporal blocks.
